source.market_name: Ahmed al-Sharaa out as leader of Syria by December 31, 2026?

market_name: Ahmed al-Sharaa out as leader of Syria by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any credible wire (Reuters/AP) reports on al-Sharaa; distinguish genuine coup/resignation news from market noise. Watch front-month Brent/WTI tick.
time_plan.1h: Compare oil move vs broad risk assets; if oil is flat while the market probability jumped, treat as noise, not leak.
time_plan.2h: Look for corroborating regional signals (Israeli/Turkish troop movements, Gulf spreads). Reassess whether a supply-relevant escalation is implied.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against energy sector and VIX; fade the thesis if no public confirmation of Syrian instability.
time_plan.12h: Close out assessment: did oil hold any risk premium? Record whether the market move preceded any public reporting.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability that al-Sharaa is removed would signal renewed instability in post-Assad Syria. Syria is a negligible oil producer, so any effect runs through a broad Middle East risk premium (fear of regional contagion, Turkish/Israeli/Iranian involvement). That channel is real but weak and diffuse; oil typically needs a direct supply threat (Strait of Hormuz, Gulf producers) to move hundreds of bps. Expected move is well below the 700bps tradable bar.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether removal odds spiked on substantive reporting; check lira (USDTRY) and TUR premarket/intraday.
time_plan.1h: Assess if Turkish move is idiosyncratic to Syria or driven by broader EM/rate news.
time_plan.2h: Watch Turkish CDS and border-region reporting for escalation signs.
time_plan.6h: Reassess; fade if no concrete Syria development surfaces publicly.
time_plan.12h: Final review of whether TUR/lira reaction tracked the market signal or was coincidental.

predictions.reasoning: Turkey is the most exposed liquid market to Syrian political outcomes: Ankara backs the new Damascus government, hosts millions of refugees, and has troops/interests in northern Syria. A spike in removal odds implying chaos could pressure Turkish assets (refugee/security costs, border risk). But the link is indirect, Turkish markets are driven mainly by domestic monetary policy and lira dynamics, and a 12h 700bps move from Syrian headlines is unlikely. Low confidence, below tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Market question on al-Sharaa remaining Syrian president through 2026
Syria's negligible role as an oil producer
Turkey's heavy political/security exposure to Syrian outcomes
General behavior of oil and EM assets to Middle East instability
uncertainty_notes: Syria has almost no direct liquid-market exposure; all channels are indirect
12h 700bps threshold is very high for diffuse geopolitical risk
Removal could be orderly/managed rather than chaotic, muting market impact
Prediction-market probability moves on this binary are often driven by speculation, not leaks

llm_justification.summary: A jump in the implied probability that al-Sharaa loses power signals renewed Syrian/Middle East instability. Syria itself has essentially no tradable asset, so the only plausible liquid proxies are a modest crude-oil regional-risk premium (USO up) and pressure on Turkish assets (TUR down) given Ankara's deep exposure. Both channels are weak and indirect; expected 12h moves fall well short of the 700bps tradable bar, so this is best treated as a low-confidence, non-tradable mapping.
key_assumptions: A market-probability spike reflects genuine instability rather than noise
Oil and Turkish assets are the least-weak liquid proxies
No direct Gulf oil-supply threat is implied by Syrian leadership change
failure_modes: Move already public — any al-Sharaa development would hit wires fast, erasing any leak edge
Weak proxy — Syria barely moves oil; oil dominated by OPEC/Hormuz, not Damascus
Reversal — prediction-market probability often mean-reverts on speculation
Orderly transition scenario produces no risk premium at all
Turkish assets driven by domestic monetary policy, swamping any Syria signal
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
